content.text: {"headline":"Approve P0 (no action): the window 14:45-19:15 is predicted at 88.6% service level, above the 80% target, at no extra cost.","why":"The morning surge came from a regional TV ad for a zero-balance savings account at 10:50. It pushed general calls to 122-124 per interval against a forecast of about 79, and service level fell to 4.8% with 48 calls abandoned. Staffing and absences are as planned, and there is no IT incident. For the disruption window of 14:45-19:15, no action is predicted to deliver 88.6% overall service level (payments 93.6%, general 84.1%) with a 2.7% abandon rate. Rest of day is predicted at 87.7%. That clears the 80% target, so no intervention or spend is needed. No escalation is flagged.","trade_offs":["P2 (campaign-targeted chat deflection) would lift the window only slightly, to 89.2% (general 86.7%, abandon 2.5%), for ₹540, and would take payments down to 91.8%.","P3 (full mitigation) gives the best result at 89.8% (general 87.5%, abandon 2.2%) but costs ₹1,788 and needs more changes: moving up to 5 agents off payments, cancelling coaching and longer break delays.","P1 costs nothing but would leave service level lower than no action, at 86.8%. It also breaks policy MOV-03, because payments would drop to 68% during 18:00-19:00, below the 70% floor. Do not use it."],"watch":"General is the tighter queue at 84.1%, so watch it in each interval. If general calls climb back towards the 11:15-11:30 levels or new-offer calls stay well above normal, switch to P2 (₹540) to deflect campaign enquiries to chat."}
